newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: British Post Office awaits Argentine bid opening.
newsitem.headline: British Post Office awaits Argentine bid opening.

text.p: The British Post Office and its partners are entering an unexpected second round of bidding for a 30-year contract to run Argentina's post office with every confidence in their proposal's quality, an official said Wednesday.
"We are confident we have a good offer to make the Argentine government and people," said David Roberts, general manager of the British Postal Consultancy Service, an arm of the British Post Office.
"Whether that offer is good enough, we will know on Thursday," he told Reuters in an interview in Buenos Aires.

The British Post Office is serving as adviser to an Argentine group that was was declared winner in an aborted bid-opening ceremony on Monday. The consortium involves two companies controlled by Grupo Macri, as well as Banco de Galicia.
The head of Macri-controlled Itron, leading the group with another Macri firm, Sideco, had already begun speaking about running the concession when the result was cancelled.

After some confusion, Arturo Puricelli, chief of Encotesa, the Argentine postal service, said the consortium's offer of a six-month fee of $51 million beat the second-highest offer by less than the minimum five percent. He said the two groups with the highest bids would have 72 hours to prepare fresh offers.

The second-highest bid was $48.5 million per half-year from Argentine companies TAC and ROMAN, together with local businessman Samuel Liberman, owner of VCC, a cable television company, and Germany's state post office as technical adviser.

The sale of the Encotesa concession has been fraught with turbulence, with three foreign groups protesting their disqualification from the bidding. At least one of them, led by Brazilian airline VASP, is suing Encotesa.
But the British Post Office's Roberts, while acknowledging the bidding procedure has brought complaints, said the contract was very attractive.

"The fact we offered $102 million per annum gives you some idea. Multiply that by the 30 years of the contract," he said, pointing out plenty of room for growth in a deregulated postal market where Encotesa handles in one year the volume that the British Post Office handles in just five days.

The winner of Thursday's second round of bid-opening, scheduled for 1600 local/1900 GMT, will take over the Argentine postal operation in September. In the last round, a minimum difference between the two bids has not been set.
